title: How to Get Out of Debt
excerpt: Debt is not just a financial state. It is a kind of bondage, and Scripture treats it as one. Here is a plan to get free, told without shame and without easy promises.
body:
"The borrower is slave to the lender." Proverbs does not soften it, and neither should we. Debt is a form of bondage. It puts a portion of your future, your labor, your peace, into someone else's hands before you have lived it. Getting out is not merely about improving your finances. It is about getting your life back.

This is not a sermon meant to shame you. Most people in debt did not get there through reckless sin. They got there through a medical bill, a lost job, a slow drift, a culture that handed them a credit limit at eighteen and called it freedom. The point is not how you got in. The point is the door out, and there is one.

## Stop the bleeding before you treat the wound

You cannot empty a boat while the hole is still open. The first move is to stop adding new debt, full stop. That means the cards come out of the wallet, the financing offers get declined, and you commit to living on what you actually earn while you fight your way clear.

This will require a real budget, the kind that gives first, provides, and tells the truth about where the money goes. If you have never done a sixty-day look at your spending, do it now. You cannot fight an enemy you refuse to count.

This stage hurts. You will say no to things, and some of those nos will feel like going backward. They are not. They are the tourniquet.

## Face the full number

Write down every debt. All of them. The card, the second card, the medical bill, the loan from your brother-in-law you have been pretending does not count. Balance, interest rate, minimum payment, the whole list.

Most people in debt avoid this exact step because the total is terrifying. But the terror lives in the vagueness. A debt you will not look at controls you precisely because it stays a shapeless dread. Named on a page, it becomes finite, a thing with edges, a thing that can be paid. I have avoided this list myself, and I can tell you the fear was always worse than the number.

## Attack in order, with everything you have

Line your debts up and pour every extra dollar at one of them while paying minimums on the rest. There are two honest ways to choose which one.

Pay the smallest balance first, regardless of interest, and you get a quick win that feeds your resolve. This is the snowball, and it works because debt is more a battle of morale than of math. Or pay the highest interest rate first, and you lose less money over time. Either is wise. The deadly mistake is spreading your effort thin across all of them and never finishing any.

When one debt is gone, take everything you were throwing at it and add it to the next. The payment grows like a stone rolling downhill. The last debts fall faster than the first.

## Bring others in

Debt thrives in secrecy. The shame keeps it hidden, and the hiddenness keeps it growing. If you are married, this is not your debt to fight alone in the dark. It is a shared wound, and it requires both of you at the table with every number visible.

And let the church be the church. The early believers in Acts did not watch each other drown. They shared what they had so that there was not a needy person among them. If you are sinking, tell someone who can pray, counsel, and sometimes help. Pride has kept more people in debt longer than interest rates ever did.

## Guard against the return

Getting out once is not the same as staying out. The same pressures that put you under will come back. So as the debt falls, build the thing that will keep you from needing it again, a margin, an emergency fund, the ant's storehouse against the winter you cannot yet see.

Freedom that is not defended gets lost. Build the wall while you are tearing down the prison.

## This week

Make the list. Every debt, every balance, every rate, on one page. Then choose your first target, smallest balance or highest rate, and find one dollar amount you can throw at it beyond the minimum this month. Cut something to get it. Tell one trusted person what you are doing so you are not fighting alone.

You will not be free this week. But the slow road out begins the moment you stop looking away from the number and start, with a real plan, to walk it. The borrower is slave to the lender. You were not made for that. Start walking home.
